headline: Light showers this evening into Monday morning give way to a warming trend, with a much warmer Thanksgiving through Saturday (a 60–80% chance of 80 degrees or more near the coast on Friday) and possible weak Santa Ana winds, while coastal flood alerts stay up on the Orange and San Diego County coasts through Thursday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Sunday stays mostly dry across coastal Carlsbad and the rest of San Diego County, with high clouds this morning and lower clouds (bases around 4,000–7,000 feet) filling in over the coast and valleys after about 10 AM; inland highs run 5 to 10 degrees below normal. A weak disturbance brings isolated to scattered light showers this evening into Monday morning from the mountains west to the coast, with the best coverage along the coast and in the San Diego County valleys. Showers could show up near Carlsbad and San Diego as early as 3 PM, are most likely there between about 9 PM and 1 AM, then taper off mainly after 4 AM, with rain totals around 0.20 inch or less. Snow levels sit near 5,500–6,500 feet, but with so little moisture the mountains get a light dusting at most.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Showers end over Orange County and the Inland Empire around sunrise Monday but linger over San Diego County through mid-morning, then land areas dry out Monday afternoon. Tuesday turns warmer and drier with a light breeze blowing off the land and a brief build of high pressure, bringing highs near normal inland and about 3 to 5 degrees above normal near the coast. Wednesday looks similar: computer models now largely agree on a passing disturbance that has trended much drier, with rain chances under 10 percent.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving through Saturday will be much warmer as high pressure builds and winds blow offshore (from the land toward the sea), with the hottest day on Friday: there is a 60–80 percent chance of highs of 80 or more in the coastal areas and lower deserts, but no chance of 90 at this time. About a quarter of model runs dig a stronger low over Arizona and Mexico on Thanksgiving, which would mean somewhat cooler weather but stronger offshore winds, while most show high pressure taking over by Friday; offshore winds peak Thursday night into Friday morning, with a 45 percent chance of weak Santa Ana winds Friday and a 25 percent chance of a weak-to-moderate event. Saturday cools slightly as winds turn back onshore, though highs stay 5 to 10 degrees above normal. Another storm could arrive late Saturday or next Sunday, but its timing and rain are very uncertain; for now it looks weak, with a 20–40 percent chance of a quarter inch or more from the coast to the mountains, and the national 8–14 day outlook gives California a 33–40 percent chance of wetter-than-normal weather into early December.

coast: A Coastal Flood Advisory covers the Orange County and San Diego County coasts until 4 AM Tuesday, followed by a Coastal Flood Watch from late Monday night through Thursday afternoon. Offshore, no marine hazards are expected through Tuesday, though a few showers may linger over the coastal waters into Monday afternoon. The next system and its swell are likely to arrive Wednesday afternoon into Thursday and could bring hazardous conditions, with gusts up to about 29 mph (25 knots) and seas of 8–12 feet, though its track and strength are still uncertain.
watch_for: Coastal Flood Advisory for the Orange and San Diego County coasts until 4 AM Tuesday, then a Coastal Flood Watch from late Monday night through Thursday afternoon.
How strong the Thursday night–Friday offshore winds get (45% chance of weak Santa Ana winds Friday) and how hot Friday turns out.
Whether the late Saturday–Sunday storm brings meaningful rain.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in light showers tonight and a dry, warmer Tuesday–Wednesday, certain that Thanksgiving through Saturday will be much warmer, but less sure how strong the offshore winds get and very uncertain about next weekend's storm.
